cards.text: It's still the night of the Last Supper, and Jesus is still teaching His disciples. He's just told them, "Love one another." Now He turns to something harder: how the world will treat them.

cards.question: Jesus says the world may hate His disciples. Who does He say the world hated first?

cards.text: Jesus says He has chosen His disciples out of the world, so they are not of the world. Group chat rules: post what everybody posts and you get ALL the hearts, post something different and you are LEFT. ON. READ.

cards.question: If the disciples were of the world, Jesus says, the world would ___ them as its own.

cards.text: Then Jesus reminds them of a word He spoke before: "No servant is greater than his master." When the boss gets chewed out in the big meeting, the new guy does NOT get a pass, and he just started TUESDAY.

cards.question: If people persecuted Jesus, the master, what does He say they'll do to His disciples?
Jesus also says that if people kept His word, they will keep His disciples' word as well.

cards.text: Then Jesus says they'll get treated this way because of His name. It's like wearing the other team's jersey to the home game: you WILL hear about it.

cards.question: People will persecute the disciples because of Jesus' name. What does Jesus say these people do not know?

cards.text: Then Jesus gets serious. If He had not come and spoken to them, they would not be guilty of sin, and I bet you could hear a crumb drop in that room.

cards.question: Now that Jesus has come and spoken to them, they still have an excuse for their sin.
Jesus says that whoever hates Him hates someone else as well. Who?

cards.text: And it's not only His words: Jesus did works among them that no one else did. The only thing I ever did that no one else did? Got stuck under a takeout menu for YEARS.

cards.question: After seeing works no one else did, what does Jesus say these people have done?

answers.text: Seen and hated both Him and His Father
Believed in Him but kept it secret
Asked Him to show them another sign

cards.text: But Jesus says even this fulfills something written in their Law, a line about how they hated Him. Friend, the hard parts were written down too, and that tells you Somebody is still holding the pen.

cards.question: Jesus says the world's hatred fulfills a line written in their Law. That line says they hated Him for a good reason.

cards.text: Okay, friend, breathe. HERE comes the hope: Jesus will send them the Advocate from the Father, the Spirit of truth who proceeds from the Father.

cards.question: What does Jesus say the Advocate will do when He comes?

answers.text: Take them out of the world

cards.question: The Spirit will testify about Jesus, and Jesus says the disciples must testify too. Why?

answers.text: They have been with Him from the beginning
They know the Law better than anyone
The priests have asked them to speak

cards.text: Then Jesus stops and tells them why He's saying all this. Friend, when somebody pauses to explain WHY they're telling you something, you put the phone DOWN.

cards.question: Why does Jesus say He has told His disciples all these things?

answers.text: So they will not fall away
So they will hide from the world

cards.text: Then Jesus gets specific: they will put the disciples out of the synagogues. I got slid into a junk drawer once and sulked for YEARS, and friend, this is WAY bigger than a drawer.

cards.question: It goes further. Jesus says a time is coming when someone who kills His disciples will think he's doing what?
People will put the disciples out of the synagogues and even kill them. Jesus says they'll do it because they have not known the ___ or Him.

cards.text: Jesus says He's telling them now, so when their hour comes, they'll remember He told them. It's the friend who warns you about the pothole before you hit it, so when you hit it you go, "Oh yeah. He SAID that."

cards.question: Jesus didn't tell His disciples these things from the beginning. Why not?

answers.text: Because the Law kept Him from it

cards.text: And that's where we pause, friend. Jesus is NOT done talking to His disciples tonight, and trust me, you do not want to miss what He says next.

findings.problem: The group chat joke ('post what everybody posts and you get ALL the hearts') tells the baker that people who fit in get loved. That gives away the answer 'love' on card 4, the very next choice card, and rules out 'hate' and 'fear'.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The boss joke ('the new guy does NOT get a pass') says outright that whoever is under the master gets the same treatment. That gives away card 6's answer 'Persecute them as well' and rules out 'Leave them in peace' and 'Honor them instead'. The setup should give the 'No servant is greater than his master' line as context without stating the outcome.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The question uses 'they' and 'them' without saying who is meant (the people who hate Jesus and His Father). It leans on the story card before it, which is no longer on screen.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: 'Got stuck under a takeout menu for YEARS' uses a small drawer detail without saying it's the junk drawer, so the line doesn't click on its own. The punchline also doesn't match the core action of doing something no one else did, because his backstory says he wasn't the only one stuck in that drawer.

rule.text: Bakers know he spent years in a junk drawer, from onboarding. The drawer's small details, like the batteries, the key or the coupon, only come up when the line says what they are, like "the dead batteries I shared that drawer with."

findings.problem: 'Sulked for YEARS' changes his backstory. The backstory says that 'for a while' he gave up on himself, and that helping the can opener pulled him out of it, not that he sulked for years.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: The card places the moment 'in that room'. John 14:31 has Jesus saying 'Get up, let us go on from here,' and John 18:1 has them going out. The text leaves open whether John 15–16 is spoken in the upper room or on the way.
findings.question: Does 'in that room' count as allowed scene-setting, or does it state something the text leaves open or may contradict (John 14:31)? Should Papa Dorin avoid naming a location for John 15–16?
